bugs.title: Smart audio level normalization (background vs vocals)
bugs.notes: Background audio currently adjusted by simple volume multiplier -> inconsistent perceived loudness. Replace with actual loudness analysis: measure background track level against vocal/narration track (ffmpeg loudnorm/volumedetect or equivalent) and adjust background so ratio is consistently background:vocals = 0.3:1 regardless of input loudness. Must be measured/calculated, not a fixed blind percentage. | [2026-08-28] Started investigation. FIXED in f3a7d65: render.py now measures EBU R128 integrated loudness (ffmpeg loudnorm print_format=json, same parse pattern voiceover.py already used) of BOTH the merged voiceover WAV and the music file, then computes music_gain_db = (voice_lufs + 10*log10(0.3)) - music_lufs so the bed lands at exactly 0.3:1 perceived loudness vs vocals regardless of source loudness. render_merged now writes the merged voiceover WAV BEFORE produce_merged_video so the real vocal track is measured; the computed linear gain replaces the fixed volume=0.33 in the music filter chain; side-chain ducking + limiter unchanged. Gain clamped [-40,+24] dB; falls back to legacy 0.33 with a WARNING only when measurement is impossible (silent/corrupt file), keeping render alive. Verified with real ffmpeg: quiet (-47.75 LUFS) -> +18.67 dB, loud (-18.35 LUFS) -> -10.73 dB; both re-measure within 0.1 dB of target. Tests: 41/41 stage_b + 175 pipeline pass; test_telegram_relay failure is PRE-EXISTING (verified identical on base commit before my change) — low-disk sandbox preflight, unrelated.
